title: Multi-region hosting risk and keystore probe with Auriga Bancorp
summary: Discovery to surface Auriga's regional residency constraints, keystore residency requirements, and logging/redaction needs. Redwood AE/SE covered Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs, KMS options, and proposed pilot steps.
next_steps: Priya to share simplified bench script and runbook link
Ethan to send draft pricing for 3-node dedicated pool and private deployment estimate
Marcus to confirm internal decision committee date and provide list of PII-sensitive flows

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-07-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Shaw (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marcus Hale (Auriga Head of Platform), Sofia Chen (Auriga Security Lead), Rajan Patel (Auriga Infrastructure)

[00:00] Ethan Shaw: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick round of intros then we can jump into the residency and keystore questions Marcus sent over.
[00:18] Marcus Hale: Thanks Ethan. Yep I'm Marcus, I'll kick off, Sofia and Rajan are on for security and infra. We've got a compliance board meeting in two weeks so trying to nail down hosting model constraints.
[00:30] Sofia Chen: Hi all. Short version, we need clear answers on where keys live, whether logs ever cross borders, and a bounded retention policy we can show auditors.
[00:41] Priya Nair: Great, thanks Sofia. We'll cover Hosted, Dedicated, and Private and highlight tradeoffs. Quick note — some names in my notes may be off, e.g., I wrote "Redwood Privatee" at one point sorry.
[00:50] Rajan Patel: No worries. First question: can Redwood Hosted guarantee logs never leave eu-west for EU workloads?
[01:05] Priya Nair: On the hosted tier we operate regional clusters and can serve traffic from eu-west, but for strict legal residency where logs must never leave EU we typically recommend either Dedicated in region or the Private deployment (VPC/on-prem). Hosted has multi-tenant control plane elements that, while not containing PII, may still have metadata that compliance teams scrutinize — so we avoid promising full evidence of non-exfiltration on hosted in strict residencies.
[01:36] Marcus Hale: So Dedicated in eu-west would keep inference and logs in region? What about control plane metadata?
[01:46] Ethan Shaw: Dedicated keeps the serving runtime and log storage in the committed region; control plane telemetry can be optioned to a regional-only configuration with export restrictions, but that requires the dedicated contract and sometimes additional attestation. We can provide a region-locking addendum.
[02:02] Sofia Chen: And KMS? We need keys to be in our KMS in our tenant — no Redwood-managed keys for the sensitive endpoints.
[02:12] Priya Nair: Under Private deployments you get customer-managed KMS integration and HSM options. For Dedicated we support bring-your-own-KMS (BYOK) via customer-managed keys, and we can set up a key policy so material never leaves. For Hosted, BYOK is more limited and there are still operational footprints that Redwood manages.
[02:33] Rajan Patel: Ok. Does BYOK with Dedicated mean Redwood never sees plaintext model inputs in our logs?
[02:41] Ethan Shaw: We can configure log minimization and redaction so PII isn't stored; if KMS is customer-controlled and encryption-at-rest keys are in your tenant, then audit evidence can show Redwood didn't have key access. However, runtime telemetry for debugging — for example trace IDs or obfuscated inputs — may still be available unless redaction rules are applied.
[03:08] Sofia Chen: We need explicit log redaction rules and proof of deletion workflows for audit. Does Redwood provide deletion playbooks?
[03:17] Priya Nair: Yes — we have an ops playbook and deletion API for Dedicated and Private. We'll share the deletion runbook link after the call (note: link in my notes is redwood.ai/ops/deletion-runbook but double-check). For Hosted, retention windows are configurable but deletion guarantees tied to multi-tenant storage have more caveats.
[03:41] Marcus Hale: Another one — legal hold. If regulators ask us to preserve all data for a subpoena, can we freeze logs in our deployment?
[03:50] Ethan Shaw: Yes for Dedicated/Private you can snapshot and place legal hold. For Hosted, we handle holds but it's less direct — you'd open a ticket and we'd coordinate.
[04:01] Rajan Patel: Network egress: are any calls to external telemetry services (third-party monitoring) made by default?
[04:10] Priya Nair: By default Redwood ships basic telemetry to our monitoring endpoint for platform health, but in Dedicated/Private we can disable external telemetry and route all metrics to customer endpoints. It's configurable per-pool.
[04:24] Sofia Chen: Can you walk us through the key escrow and rotation model if we need long-term escrow for compliance?
[04:33] Priya Nair: Briefly: we support a key-escrow workflow where customer keys can be escrowed in a customer-chosen HSM vendor; Redwood integrates with that HSM for key unwrap but never stores plaintext. Rotation is supported; we can provide rotation audit logs. For higher-assurance requirements we recommend Private + HSM.
[04:53] Marcus Hale: Sounds good. On the hosting cost side — what is the rough delta between Hosted and a small Dedicated pool? We're trying to justify budget to finance.
[05:03] Ethan Shaw: For a 3-node GPU pool in region, rough rule of thumb is Hosted is pay-per-use so variable; Dedicated would be an annual reserved commit — typically 30–60% higher than top-line hosted for baseline but gives predictable throughput and region-locking. I'll put numbers in the follow-up.
[05:22] Rajan Patel: Ok. On latency: we have EU clients but also US-based microservices that call the inference APIs. If we lock region to eu-west, will US services see increased latencies?
[05:33] Priya Nair: Yes, cross-region traffic will add RTT. We recommend edge routing or a hybrid where non-sensitive calls go to hosted US while sensitive calls route to EU dedicated. Redwood supports policy-based routing per endpoint.
[05:49] Sofia Chen: For GDPR specifically, if we do Dedicated in eu-west, do we still need data processing agreements?
[05:58] Ethan Shaw: Yes, DPA still applies. We'll provide a DPA that maps processing activities and subprocessors. For Private (VPC/on-prem) the relationship is more of a software license and the DPA reflects customer control.
[06:12] Marcus Hale: I'd like to surface one of our tricky flows — batch ingestion of KYC docs. Those are heavy PII and are currently processed in our us-east pipelines. We want to stop that from touching US infra. Can Redwood pipeline into a region-locked ingest?
[06:27] Priya Nair: You can either stage ingestion in-region via Private/Dedicated, or use our ingestion proxy to route and redact upstream. There are tradeoffs: redaction at ingestion can preserve SLOs but requires careful eval of false negatives.
[06:42] Rajan Patel: Are there existing customers who've done EU-only Dedicated with BYOK? We want references for the board.
[06:49] Ethan Shaw: Yes — we can share anonymized case studies and compliance attestations. I'll send a short list.
[06:55] Sofia Chen: How about audit logs granularity? We need per-token anonymized metrics and per-request metadata for forensics.
[07:04] Priya Nair: Audit logs for Dedicated/Private include per-request headers, request/response size (not raw tokens unless enabled), timestamps, and model variant. Token-level logs are considered high-sensitivity; we offer token sampling or redaction to mitigate.
[07:21] Marcus Hale: For legal discovery, do you support export in standard formats?
[07:26] Ethan Shaw: Yes, logs can be exported in JSON lines or CSV with PII redaction applied. There's an export job we can run with retention annotations.
[07:35] Rajan Patel: One operational ask: our infra team wants the option to run a small pilot in our GCP eu-west zone then compare to a Redwood Private appliance. How long to provision a Private on-prem package?
[07:47] Priya Nair: On-prem packages typically take 4–8 weeks for air-gapped installs (including compliance checks). VPC-private deployments in cloud regions can be faster — 2–3 weeks depending on networking.
[07:59] Marcus Hale: Are there any opt-in features that would leak metadata like tenant identifiers outside region?
[08:08] Priya Nair: Not by default. Certain optional features like aggregated usage analytics may be routed to central telemetry — we can opt you out. We'll surface the small exceptions in the technical appendix.
[08:22] Ethan Shaw: Quick interruption — Sofia, you mentioned wanting proof-of-deletion workflows. We'll include the deletion playbook and a sample audit extract. Priya will share the runbook link.
[08:34] Sofia Chen: Thanks. Also can you confirm SSO options? We use SAML with an internal IdP and need SCIM provisioning.
[08:42] Priya Nair: SAML SSO and SCIM are supported for Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we support SAML SSO but SCIM provisioning depends on the account model. We'll make a table for you.
[08:55] Marcus Hale: One more thing: data residency of derivative outputs. Say we send PII and get back classification labels — are those outputs stored?
[09:05] Priya Nair: Outputs follow the same retention rules. If you mark a flow as sensitive, we can route both inputs and outputs to the region-bound store and apply redaction.
[09:16] Rajan Patel: Benchmarks — what should we run? We have a mix of chat-like prompts and batch embedding jobs.
[09:25] Priya Nair: We'll share a small bench script that measures p95 latency for generation at typical prompt lengths and throughput for embedding batches. We'll also include a KV-cache hit-rate test for chat flows. Expect the script to be lightweight — run for <1 hour.
[09:40] Marcus Hale: Great. On the compliance docs, do you have SOC 2 report and ISO27001?
[09:47] Ethan Shaw: Yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 — we'll send redacted reports and the latest summary.
[09:55] Sofia Chen: Anything else around encryption in transit? We need TLS mutual auth for internal tooling.
[10:02] Priya Nair: Mutual TLS is supported for Private/VPC. For Dedicated we can configure mTLS between client and serving endpoint. Hosted supports standard TLS; mTLS is restricted.
[10:14] Marcus Hale: Ok thanks. This was useful.
[10:18] Ethan Shaw: Quick recap of commitments: Priya will share bench script and runbook links; I'll email initial pricing and reference list; Marcus will share sensitive flow list and decision timeline.
[10:29] Rajan Patel: I'll coordinate the pilot infra.
[10:33] Sofia Chen: And I'll prepare the board packet with the DPA callouts.
[10:36] Ethan Shaw: Perfect. I'll send the follow-up and create a stub SOW for the dedicated pilot option.
[10:41] Marcus Hale: Thanks everyone.

References noted during call:
- deletion runbook (Priya): redwood.ai/ops/deletion-runbook (confirm link)
- bench script (to be shared)
- SOC 2 / ISO summaries (to be attached)

End of transcript.
